title: Haus Citrus Flower Aperitif
about: Haus was founded in Sonoma County in 2019 by Helena Price Hambrecht, who had spent years building brands for Silicon Valley companies, and her husband Woody Hambrecht, a Sonoma winemaker and grape grower. Their idea was a lower-alcohol aperitif, made largely from fruit and botanicals grown on the family’s Healdsburg ranch and sold directly to drinkers. Citrus Flower was the first release, and it sold out within twelve hours. In 2023 the San Francisco company The Naked Market acquired the brand and relaunched it with Citrus Flower among its core bottlings, with Sonoma winemaker Micah Wirth leading winemaking.

Haus is wine-based and technically classed as a vermouth. At launch Citrus Flower was built on a Chardonnay base, fortified with grape brandy infused with elderflower, lemon, grapefruit, hibiscus and cinnamon, and lightly sweetened with cane sugar; the brand claimed far less sugar than its European counterparts. In its early years Haus made and bottled the aperitif in a small warehouse just north of the Hambrechts’ farm, where Woody also managed sixty-seven acres of wine grapes.

The current bottling is described as crisp and refreshing, led by lemon with subtle elderflower and a hint of cinnamon. It drinks well on its own over ice, or lengthened into a spritz with club soda or prosecco.
facts: Over ice, or with club soda or prosecco
